description: Table of contents of a 10-K / 10-Q / 8-K (or 10-K/A, 10-Q/A, 8-K/A) so an agent can read the filing's WORDS: returns the form, filing/period/acceptance dates, the primary-document URL, and every section found with its `key`, `title`, `char_count` and a short `first_line`. 10-K keys are the Item numbers (1, 1A, 1B, 1C, 2-6, 7, 7A, 8, 9, 9A, 9B, 9C, 10-16 when present); 10-Q keys are I-1..I-4 and II-1, II-1A, II-2, II-5, II-6; financial-statement notes are `note-N` (listed separately under `notes`; a filer that puts its statements under Item 15 has them there); an amendment opens with `explanatory-note`. 8-K keys are its Item numbers (`2.02` results, `5.02` officers and directors, `7.01` Regulation FD, `8.01` other events, `9.01` exhibits; `5`, `7`, `12` on filings before August 2004) and each EX-99 exhibit (the press release or letter the event is told in) is its own section `ex-99.1`, `ex-99.2`, with its own `source_url`; `unread_documents` names any EX-99 exhibit not included (too large, missing, or past the first 4) with its EDGAR URL. `document` is always listed last: the whole filing text (an 8-K's exhibits included), paged like any section. Read it when an Item is only a page pointer (a cross-reference-index 10-K: "Item 7 | Pages 45-90") or missing; nothing in the filing is out of reach. PROVENANCE: this is TEXT, not figures. A number read in a section is NOT a Valuein figure. Cite it as "stated in {form} {accession_id}, {section}" and never mint a fact_id or compute from it; figures come from the fact tools. Find accession numbers with get_sec_filing_links, then call read_filing_section; to find a statement, note or phrase without paging, call find_in_filing. PIT-safe: a filing is its own as-of date; pass `as_of_date` to refuse a filing accepted after it. Coverage follows the plan (sample: S&P 500 sample, 5 years; Benchmark: S&P 500; Pro: from 2011; Institutional: everything). Read-only; fetched from SEC EDGAR once per accession and cached.

accession.description: EDGAR accession number of the 10-K / 10-Q / 8-K, e.g. '0000320193-19-000119'. Take it from get_sec_filing_links.

as_of_date.description: Point-in-time guard (YYYY-MM-DD). A filing is its own as-of: if it was accepted by the SEC after this date the call is refused rather than reading text that did not exist yet.

ticker.description: Stock ticker, e.g. AAPL — or a CIK (SEC identifier), e.g. '0000320193'. A CIK is the stable identifier.

name: list_filing_sections

_meta.description: Provenance envelope — data lineage for every MCP response

cost_usd.description: Per-call cost transparency. Omitted for subscription-only and free tools, which have no MPP price.

basis.description: mpp_charge = real pay-per-call charge (a card or MPP payment through agent-pay). mpp_rate_card = indicative price, not billed.

billed.description: true = this amount was actually charged via MPP for this call. false = indicative MPP-equivalent value only: no charge was made for this call (it was within your plan).

data_plan.description: Access plan: sample | sp500 | pro | full

data_quality.description: Server-side invariants run on this response

fundamentals_as_of.description: ISO timestamp when the FINANCIAL STATEMENTS were last rebuilt in bulk. Use THIS — not `last_updated` — when telling a user how current the cross-sectional fundamentals are. The snapshot is republished on every weekday price refresh while the statements are carried forward unchanged, so `last_updated` can be far more recent than the numbers it sits next to. It is a floor for a single filer, not a ceiling: a filer with a live partition receives its filing, facts and ratios intraday (minutes after EDGAR dissemination), so an entity-scoped read may carry a filing newer than this; cross-sectional ranks (factor scores, earnings signals) refresh with the weekly bulk export.

last_updated.description: ISO timestamp when the snapshot was exported

latency_ms.description: Wall-clock milliseconds this tool call took, measured server-side around the handler.

limit_warnings.description: Soft-warning array for partial fulfillment. Each entry carries a stable subcode + remediation.options[]. AI agents pattern-match on subcode.

mpp_offer.description: Present when figures still need payment: the MPP option (price, resource_url, request body) for the full run.

mpp_override.description: Set when this single response was paid for over MPP (card, agent-pay): the payment's order was honoured for this call only. agent-pay captures the payment only when this is present.

mpp_verification.description: Verification tools only, when some figures are outside the caller's plan. Figures the plan covers are always verified free; a Valuein account also verifies its first figures free, once, figures outside its plan included (the verification trial, size in pricing://current). served_free = own-plan figures plus trial figures; trial_used / trial_remaining = this run's draw and what the account has left; needs_payment = figures still to pay for (the paid verification run). A guest has no trial: note says how to get it.

pit_safe.description: true iff a zero-look-ahead point-in-time cut was applied to every returned figure

price_as_of.description: ISO timestamp when the price surfaces were last refreshed.

reset_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the window resets

truncation.description: Set when fewer rows were returned than requested — explains why and points to a remedy

source_url.description: The EDGAR document an exhibit section (`ex-99.N`) was read from; absent on sections of the main document.
The EDGAR document an exhibit section (`ex-99.N`) was read from; absent on sections of the main document.
The EDGAR document the text was read from.

unread_documents.description: 8-K exhibits the index lists that the text does not include; empty when every one was read.

reason.description: too_large: past the reading limit; not_found: listed but missing on EDGAR; over_limit: past the exhibits read per filing; no_text: no readable text.

source_url.description: Open the exhibit here: it is NOT in the text this tool serves.
